sec: Urine anion gap and ammonia formation · p823

items.q: Fill up: Urine anion gap = urinary Na⁺ + urinary K⁺ − ______.
items.exp: UAG = urinary Na⁺ + urinary K⁺ − urinary Cl⁻ = unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation. (Book p823)

items.q: The urine anion gap is best described as:
opts: Slightly negative, being unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation
Strongly positive, being unmeasured cation − unmeasured anion
Always zero because urine is electroneutral
Equal to the serum anion gap
items.exp: The urine anion gap (urinary Na⁺ + K⁺ − Cl⁻ = unmeasured anion − unmeasured cation) is slightly negative normally. (Book p823)

items.q: Match the urine anion gap result to its significance — 1) Positive UAG  2) Negative UAG  3) Normal UAG … A) Slightly negative  B) GI loss  C) RTA
items.exp: UAG significance: positive → RTA; negative → GI loss. (Book p823)

items.q: A patient with a normal anion gap acidosis has a negative urine anion gap. Where is the bicarbonate being lost?
items.exp: A negative urine anion gap points to GI loss; a positive gap points to renal tubular acidosis. (Book p823)

items.q: ‘Ammonia formation occurs predominantly in the proximal tubules.’
opts: True — the note states formation of ammonia is predominantly in the proximal tubules
False — ammonia is made mainly in the distal tubule
False — ammonia is made mainly in the collecting duct
True, but only during metabolic alkalosis
items.exp: Note: formation of ammonia is predominantly in the proximal tubules; the reaction chain is glutamine → glutamate → α-keto glutarate. (Book p823)

items.q: Match the ammonia-forming pathway — 1) Starting amino acid  2) First product  3) Second product … A) Glutamine  B) α-keto glutarate  C) Glutamate
items.exp: Glutamine → glutamate → α-keto glutarate, with NH₃ released at each step. (Book p823)

items.q: How many NH₃ molecules are shown being released along the printed pathway?
opts: Two — one from glutamine and one from glutamate
None — NH₃ is released only in the distal tubule
items.exp: The pathway glutamine → glutamate → α-keto glutarate shows an NH₃ released at each of the two steps. (Book p823)

items.q: A patient with diarrhoea has a normal anion gap acidosis. Which urine anion gap and ammonia pattern do you expect?
opts: Negative UAG with a brisk proximal ammonia response
Positive UAG with a blunted ammonia response
Negative UAG with a blunted ammonia response
Positive UAG with a brisk proximal ammonia response
items.exp: GI loss gives a negative urine anion gap and, unlike RTA, the proximal tubules respond by making more ammonia from glutamine. (Book p823)

items.q: All but one of these are printed in the urine anion gap section. Which is the odd one out?
opts: A positive UAG indicates gastrointestinal loss of bicarbonate
UAG = urinary Na⁺ + urinary K⁺ − urinary Cl⁻
Ammonia formation occurs predominantly in the proximal tubules
items.exp: A positive UAG indicates RTA; it is the *negative* UAG that indicates GI loss. (Book p823)
